# Power BI report specification (original plan, superseded)

**Superseded.** The report is now built. Open `MumbaiHealth.pbip`, and see `POWERBI_GUIDE.md` for how to open, publish and
embed it. The built report covers this plan's facility measures and charts, plus the cardiovascular models and the clinical
data, on five pages. The text below is kept as the original design record.

Everything needed to build the original three-page report is in this folder:

* `data/*.csv`: import-ready tables generated by `run_pipeline.py`
* `measures.dax`: all DAX measures
* `data/expected_kpis.json`: the values the finished report must reproduce

## 1. Import

Use Get Data → Text/CSV for each file in `powerbi/data/`. Set the data types below; all other columns can stay
as detected.

| Table | Key | Type fixes |
|---|---|---|
| `dim_ward` | `ward_id` (text, unique, 24 rows) | `population_2011` whole number; rates decimal; `cluster_label` whole number |
| `dim_cluster` | `cluster_label` (unique, 4 rows) | |
| `dim_category` | `category` (unique, 4 rows) | sort `category_label` by `sort_order` |
| `dim_site` | `site_id` (unique, 402 rows) | `longitude`/`latitude` decimal, Data category = Longitude/Latitude |
| `fact_facility` | `facility_id` (456 rows) | lon/lat as above; `coordinates_approximate` true/false |
| `fact_ward_category` | (`ward_id`, `category`) | |
| `ml_k_evaluation` | – (disconnected) | |

Set `dim_ward[ward_name]` to sort by `dim_ward[ward_order]`.

## 2. Relationships (all single direction, one-to-many)

```
dim_cluster[cluster_label] 1 ──► * dim_ward[cluster_label]
dim_ward[ward_id]          1 ──► * fact_facility[ward_id]
dim_ward[ward_id]          1 ──► * fact_ward_category[ward_id]
dim_category[category]     1 ──► * fact_facility[category]
dim_category[category]     1 ──► * fact_ward_category[category]
dim_site[site_id]          1 ──► * fact_facility[site_id]
```

Do **not** relate `dim_site` to `dim_ward`; the second filter path would make the model ambiguous. Use
`fact_facility[ward_id]` for ward context on sites.

**Distinct-site counting.** A site with both a dispensary and a UPHC is one row in `dim_site` and two rows in
`fact_facility`. `[Total Distinct Sites]` uses `DISTINCTCOUNT(fact_facility[site_id])`. With a category filter it
returns the sites offering that category, and with no filter it returns 402. Category bars therefore sum to 456,
not 402. Say so in a visible note.

## 3. Pages

### Page 1 – Mumbai Healthcare Overview
* Cards: `[Total Distinct Sites]` (402), `[Population 2011]` (12,442,373), `[Sites per 100k]` (3.23),
  `[Facility Records]` (456).
* Clustered bar: `dim_category[category_label]` × `[Facility Records]`.
* Map visual (Azure Maps or Map): `fact_facility` latitude/longitude, legend = `category_label`,
  tooltip = `facility_name`, `ward_id`, `coordinates_approximate`. Subtitle: "Most coordinates rounded to ~1 km."
  For ward shading, either convert `data/processed/ward_boundaries.geojson` to TopoJSON (e.g. mapshaper) for the
  Shape Map visual keyed on `ward_id`, or embed `outputs/figures/09_facility_map.png` as an image.
* Table: ward, population, sites, sites per 100k, share gap.
* Text box with the observations from Section 7 of the final report, and the data-date caveat
  (facilities 2025 vs population 2011).

### Page 2 – Ward-Level Provision Analysis
* Slicers (one row at the top): `dim_ward[ward_name]`, `dim_category[category_label]`, `dim_cluster[cluster_label]`.
* Bar charts sorted descending: `[Sites per 100k]` by ward, with a constant line at `[City-wide Sites per 100k]`;
  `[Population per Site]` by ward.
* Scatter: X = `[Population 2011]`, Y = `[Total Distinct Sites]`, details = `ward_id`.
* Diverging bar: `[Share Gap (pp)]` by ward (conditional colour: > 0 red `#e34948`, < 0 blue `#2a78d6`).
* Stacked bar: `fact_ward_category[facility_records]` by ward and category.
* **Drill-through page "Ward detail"**: drill-through field `dim_ward[ward_id]`. Show cards for
  `[Selected Ward Label]`, population, sites, sites per 100k, share gap, cluster name; a table of
  `fact_facility` (name, category, address, assignment_check); and a category bar.
* Tooltip page: ward name, population, sites per 100k, cluster name.

### Page 3 – ML Cluster Analysis
* Cards: number of clusters (4), silhouette 0.316. Text: `[Model Note]`.
* Bar: `dim_cluster[cluster_label]` × `dim_cluster[n_wards]`, tooltip `wards`.
* Table: `dim_ward` ward_id, cluster_label, cluster_name, silhouette_sample.
* Clustered bar of cluster means: from `dim_cluster`, `dispensary_per_100k_mean`, `uphc_per_100k_mean`,
  `public_hospital_per_100k_mean`, `maternity_hospital_per_100k_mean`.
* Line charts from `ml_k_evaluation`: inertia by k, silhouette by k (mark k = 4).
* Visible note: "Exploratory; 24 observations; K chosen by documented judgement (see model card); clusters are
  sensitive to feature choice; not a measure of access."
* Optional: `cluster_k2_label` as an alternative slicer.

## 4. Acceptance checks (do these after building)

| Check | Expected |
|---|---|
| Total Distinct Sites, no filters | 402 |
| Facility Records, no filters | 456 (UPHC 211, dispensary 186, hospital 31, maternity 28) |
| Population 2011 | 12,442,373 |
| Sites per 100k | 3.23 |
| Ward A: sites, per 100k | 11, 5.95 |
| Ward R/S: per 100k, share gap | 2.17, +1.82 |
| Category = Dispensary, Total Distinct Sites | 186 |
| Cluster slicer = 4 | wards A, E |
| Sum of Share Gap over all wards | 0 |

Values are taken from `data/expected_kpis.json` and `data/processed/ward_indicators.csv`. If any check fails,
the relationships or filter directions are wrong.

## 5. Theme

Use the same palette as the static figures: categories in the order dispensary `#2a78d6`, UPHC `#eb6834`,
hospital `#1baf7a`, maternity `#eda100`; sequential blues for rates; red/blue only for the share gap.
